::: {.flashcard-page}

This is a very short card about a tiny function I still find useful. After a
few hours of coding, I sometimes want Rust to tell me the concrete type of a
value without making me hover through an IDE or deliberately provoke the
compiler.

::: {.flashcard-stage}
::: {.flashcard-card}
<div class="flashcard-meta">
  <span class="flashcard-number">Flashcard 06</span>
  <span class="flashcard-topic">Rust</span>
</div>

<div class="flashcard-eyebrow">The question</div>

::: {#flashcard-question .flashcard-question role="heading" aria-level="2"}
How can I print the concrete type of a Rust value?
:::

<p class="flashcard-hint">The standard library already knows the type name. A generic helper can expose it.</p>

<details class="flashcard-reveal">
  <summary>Reveal the answer</summary>
<div class="flashcard-answer"><p>Pass a reference into a generic function and print <code>std::any::type_name::&lt;T&gt;()</code>.</p></div>
</details>
:::
:::

## The helper

```rust
use std::any::type_name;

fn what_type<T>(_: &T) {
    println!("type is: {}", type_name::<T>());
}
```

The argument gives Rust a concrete `T`. The function does not need the value
itself, so the parameter is named `_`. `type_name::<T>()` returns the name of
that type as a string slice.

## Use it with a few values

```rust
fn main() {
    let number = 3232;
    let name = "Rahul".to_string();
    let list_of_nums = vec![1, 2];

    what_type(&number);
    what_type(&name);
    what_type(&list_of_nums);
}
```

```text
type is: i32
type is: alloc::string::String
type is: alloc::vec::Vec<i32>
```

Before I knew this helper, I sometimes used IDE introspection or deliberately
assigned a value to `()` so the compiler would complain and reveal the real
type. This is a little less silly.

::: {.flashcard-block .flashcard-block--remember}
<p class="flashcard-block-label">What I keep in my head</p>

`type_name::<T>()` is useful for debugging and learning. The exact string is
intended for diagnostics, so I would not build program logic around its
format.
:::
